notes:
**The order pad showed two-fifths of what a trade costs.** "Approx charges" priced only the order being placed. On options the entry pays no STT at all and the exit pays 0.15% of premium, so the number you read before committing money was well under half the round trip. The pad now says what the whole trade costs and how far the price has to move before you are square - which is the line that makes the case: a NIFTY option lot needs most of a rupee just to break even, and a five-rupee weekly needs several percent.

**A VWAP on an index is not a VWAP.** NIFTY is a number, not something that trades, so every bar reports zero volume and the "volume-weighted" average weighs them all the same. It still runs - going silent would be worse - but the report now says so, in amber, right under the numbers.

**Which day it is, for a contract, is a question about Mumbai.** Expiry-day detection, the futures list and near-month selection all read your device's calendar. Expiry day is the one session where an option's fill model changes.

*If you skipped 0.9.83: your journal was counting trades that lost money as wins, and the coach was doing the same.*
